scope: artist-owned native per-family identity sources; no physics or RNG

grammar.silhouette: Central physical impact and outward pressure teeth
grammar.motion: Contact flash, spreading pressure fronts, staggered counter-pressure plates, fading chips
grammar.location: At the actual heavy contact point near the floor
grammar.palette: Cyan pressure, pale steel, sparse amber contact teeth
grammar.feature: Strong original ring composition; Rank II adds a second structural pressure response

impact_wake.notes: Rank I card preserves the original five editable layer cels and six accepted poses, each held for two half-duration keys. Rank I runtime must retain original 128px pressure tag in power_fx_002b.aseprite; no new wake tag is supplied so renderer falls through. New wake_ii is a structural counter-pressure response, not an enlarged recolour. Original source master retained intact.

grammar.silhouette: Preserved off-centre native metal rotor with coherent red heat arcs and restrained star accents.
grammar.motion: Authored rotor arcs and directional heat streaks; preserved stars and machine; no disconnected rectangular chip blocks.
grammar.location: Rotor edges and actual velocity wake; recoil near the floor.
grammar.persistence: Only real active/overcap/heat states; discrete ignition, commitment, strike and vent events.
grammar.palette: Oxide, hot orange, red and pale key flashes against cold steel.
grammar.feature: Open machine centre, physical rotor heat and tangential streaks; mutations retain their distinct action stories.

redline.notes: 003A.1 human correction retains stars, native main rotor and card timing. Heat blocks are replaced with coherent rotor arcs; gameplay keeps its accepted expanding red ring.

grammar.silhouette: Accepted round blade, ratchet and contact bit compressed against a physical arena wall.
grammar.motion: Wall-side squeeze, abruptly separated flight positions, violent contact and short scrape aftermath.
grammar.location: Wall contact, actual rebound vector, then target contact and floor scars.
grammar.persistence: Armed wall-rebound lifetime plus bounded charge/contact/aftermath events.
grammar.palette: Cold iron, silver, brass and small white/gold contact flashes.
grammar.feature: The whole top survives every compression, launch, target-contact and recoil beat; never a wedge.

notes: Rank II adds a second wall-side compression beat and heavier path fragments, never a larger surrounding aura.
Charge cels leave the machine centre open. Card stack height visibly compresses; runtime may compress cosmetic stack only, preserving collision geometry.

Final dense-motion correction removes opaque whole-top ghost bodies, dark supports/shadows and continuous speed bars. Runtime keeps only sparse faded true native blade-rim clusters; live top remains dominant.

grammar.silhouette: Recognizable heavy spinning top pressing its bit into fractured arena floor
grammar.motion: Settles under load; planted contact holds, Counterweight returns the accepted strike
grammar.location: Actual bit and floor; finite accepted-contact and counterstroke direction
grammar.persistence: Existing anchor and stored-force stages; bounded paid impact/release
grammar.palette: Accepted Bastion steel, sparse floor silver and restrained amber counterstroke
grammar.feature: Floor load and real rotor survival without clamp legs, platform or spring cylinder

notes: All historical Centre card/icon/FX sources inspected; older four legs and spring box were not restored.
Card subject uses accepted native Bastion/Breaker blade, ratchet and bit without resampling.
Six excellent top/load/contact poses held twice; saved editable masters are export authority.
FX show uneven physical floor seams at the actual bit with charge-stage intensity; no platform.
Bulwark remains planted after incoming contact; Counterweight returns actual accepted force.
No mechanics, charge, RPM, positions, timers or target selection changed.

grammar.silhouette: Accepted native Vane top at core-card scale, sparse actual trail, physical closure socket
grammar.motion: Route is drawn behind motion, aged crossing snaps locally, Ghost sockets meet and the actual path locks
grammar.location: Recorded routes, endpoints and actual crossing points
grammar.persistence: Bounded route history plus finite latch/crossing responses
grammar.palette: Sparse cyan and ice scars; Ghost uses green mechanical route teeth
grammar.feature: The route occupies the illustration and gameplay space; Ghost closure and Slipstream crossing have different spatial and timing language

afterimage.notes: 003A.1 human correction adopts the quiet core-card framing and accepted native machine anatomy. Ghost route and Slipstream crossing retain distinct identities. Layers/tags/pivots/authored milliseconds preserved.

grammar.silhouette: Three recognizable spinning tops in the restored triangular collision relay
grammar.motion: First contact expands locally; actual receivers react sequentially
grammar.location: Paid collision/elimination source and snapshotted real recipients
grammar.persistence: Finite 0.38s event; at most three native cels, no persistent player aura
grammar.palette: Accepted warm orange/gold collision clusters and steel tops
grammar.feature: Historical triangular top story plus causal source-to-recipient contact reactions

chain_impact.notes: Restores bdcc24e card layers and independent icon Rank I exactly; six poses and total duration preserved through paired holds. Rank II develops the final contact without changing composition. Original native128 pressure source plus at most two real recipient contact cels retain the current three-cel draw bound. Receiver metadata and physics are untouched.

grammar.silhouette: Accepted wobbling blade and ratchet on a visibly scraping bit, followed by a small physical floor catch.
grammar.motion: Uneven scrape, loaded bit bite, and the same top settling back upright.
grammar.location: One side of the low bearing and contact-floor scrape.
grammar.persistence: Intermittent actual danger window; bounded successful-contact catch.
grammar.palette: Dull steel/brass, small gold tooth tips, oxide strain marks and one pale catch flash.
grammar.feature: The top itself leans and catches; one tiny floor bite replaces the detached bearing device.

notes: Rank II adds a second small redirected catch fragment, never a separate supporting device.
The authored catch never resets the physical player, reserve, collision radius or position.

grammar.silhouette: Recognisable native top plus physically separated round rotor echoes; Flow retains an open contact path.
grammar.motion: Sparse native rim fragments separate as thrust rises. Terminal opens longer gaps; Flow retains three disconnected bent floor groups.
grammar.location: Sparse rear blade-rim memories along the actual velocity; the real live top stays dominant.
grammar.persistence: Moving speed state; terminal surge is event-based.
grammar.palette: Steel, ice and cool blue; muted mint retained rails; sparse terminal brass tips.
grammar.feature: Terminal separated blade-tip glints versus Flow short bent floor groups remain distinct in grayscale; no opaque rack or rail.

notes: Rank II adds one further sparse blade-rim memory; no housing, filled base, shadow block or continuous speed bars.
Flow preserves a long open floor-contact bend. Orbit instead cuts a compact concave hook and ejects grit.

Final dense-motion correction removes opaque whole-top ghost bodies, dark supports/shadows and continuous speed bars. Runtime keeps only sparse faded true native blade-rim clusters; live top remains dominant.

grammar.silhouette: Accepted physical top travelling around a broad C-shaped contact-tip route.
grammar.motion: Enter turn, cut a growing outside hook, throw grit and release the arc.
grammar.location: Floor/contact point outside the turn, below the rotor.
grammar.persistence: Only actual brake-turn drift/arc state; scuffs settle after the carving beat.
grammar.palette: Worn steel floor scars, muted teal edge and brass grit.
grammar.feature: One short concave floor cut with displaced outer grit; no rotor aura or long Flow rails.

notes: Rank II deepens two outside skid grooves and ejects extra grit, staying at the contact plane.

grammar.silhouette: round actual defender top receives an angular incoming top
grammar.motion: contact bends at the blade, defender yields slightly, attacker redirects
grammar.location: genuine incoming blade rim and local recoil skid
grammar.palette: accepted blue steel defender against red attacker and short silver rim pressure
grammar.feature: absorption and redirected displacement without piston, box or shield device

notes: Six strong card poses occupy twelve keyed frames through explicit two-key holds.
Card bodies copy exact accepted starter_blade_accents_002b1 native cels and the accepted bit/ratchet parts, without resizing or recolouring.
Rank II develops physical force and travel marks rather than adding a device.
Icons are separately authored recognizable miniature tops and travel/contact.
FX omit replacement bodies, gadgets and synthetic particles; real gameplay tops remain visible.
All eight projected headings have eight authored native keys. Existing gameplay fields/events remain authoritative.
Historical internal tag damper_contact now means a short physical blade absorption/redirect response, with no piston or device pixels.

grammar.location: actual top heel and floor; release follows its real movement vector
grammar.persistence: empty stage zero; visible earned charge stages one through seven plus existing store/release events
grammar.palette: accepted blue Bastion steel body, restrained brass and pale floor wakes
grammar.feature: one recognizable top and compressed physical floor travel; no detached cassette
